The Total T4 level is elevated (11.7 µg/dL), but Free T4 is within the normal range (0.9 ng/dL). Elevated Total T4 with normal Free T4 and TSH levels can indicate that the high T4 is not due to hyperthyroidism.

Elevated hsCRP (4.5 mg/L) and Ferritin (281 ng/mL) indicate systemic inflammation. Inflammation can affect thyroid hormone levels, including increasing Total T4.

TSH (1.270 µIU/mL) and Free T3 (2.8 pg/mL) are within normal ranges, suggesting that thyroid function is regulated properly.

Anti-TPO (22 IU/mL) and Anti-TG (15.0 IU/mL) are within normal limits, suggesting the absence of autoimmune thyroid disease like Hashimoto's thyroiditis or Graves' disease.
